text:
maria: bringing up raptor65b (int4) on dedicated pool — hitting OOMs and p99 spikes after ~30k tokens of steady traffic. memory fragmentation looks suspicious, and kv cache growth seems higher than expected. saw 1/8 pods crash within 10m. uploading logs now :point_up:

aj: can you paste the deploy config you used? curious about max_new_tokens + batch defaults

maria: sure — small snippet:
```
model: raptor65b-int4
batching:
  max_batch_size: 8
  max_tokens_per_batch: 2048
defaults:
  max_new_tokens: 256
  prefetch_kv: true
```

maria: logs show repeated allocation failures then long GC pauses, then OOM. Fragmentation counters: anon_frag_ratio ~0.42 after 20m (normally ~0.12).

suhas: 0.42 is super high. did quantizer change the allocator pattern? which quant backend?

maria: used our new micro-quantizer (int4-fused) from the onboarding patch. local bench looked fine, but production TL;DR: slower KV trims and slightly larger per-layer buffers.

leo: can we try lowering max_new_tokens to 128 and reduce max_batch_size to 4 as an experiment? reduces peak working set and evicts KV more frequently.

priya: also suggest disabling prefetch_kv for a canary group — might avoid overallocating contiguous arenas that fragment.

aj: +1 to canary. also add a periodic kv-prune every 5s for the canary to keep cache bounded.

maria: rolling a canary now with: max_new_tokens=128, max_batch_size=4, prefetch_kv=false, kv_prune_interval=5s. will update in ~10m.

infra-bot: canary deploy started for raptor65b-int4 on pool gpu-dedicated-11 (ids: pod-2304..pod-2307)

maria: first 15m: no crashes. p50/p95 latency slightly higher (~+5ms) but p99 dropped ~150ms. fragmentation dropped to ~0.18. memory RSS per pod down ~12%.

leo: interesting — latency trade looks fine for reliability. any quality diffs with max_new_tokens=128?

maria: ran our eval harness (1000 prompts sampled from prod) — no measurable quality reg regression (ROUGE / BLEU stable within noise).

aj: can you also try a mid approach: max_new_tokens=192, max_batch_size=6, prefetch_kv=true but kv_prune_interval=3s — to see if we can recover some latency without reintroducing frag.

maria: launching mid-run now.

maria: mid-run update (10m): 1 pod hit high anon_frag_ratio ~0.31 but didn't OOM. p99 slightly noisier, occasionally back to pre-change levels. overall RSS up ~6% vs canary.

priya: maybe this indicates prefetch_kv is the main factor for fragmentation when combined with larger batches. we should document a safe default for onboarding int4: max_new_tokens=128, max_batch_size=4, prefetch_kv=false, kv_prune_interval=5s.

leo: agree. could we also add an allocator hint in the quant build to use smaller arenas for KV to reduce fragmentation? open a ticket to runtime team?

aj: I filed INF-8723 with the runtime team, linking profiler dumps and the quant patch. tagging @suhas for kernel selection follow-up.

suhas: saw the ticket, will investigate kernel allocation patterns and whether jemalloc tunables can help for this quant flavor. quick idea: enable jemalloc background_thread and aggressive purging for pools running int4 models.

maria: action items: 
- ship onboarding default changes for raptor65b-int4 (maria)
- add canary test to onboarding checklist (priya)
- runtime ticket INF-8723 (aj -> suhas)
- perf/eval run to re-check quality after 24h (maria)

maria: plan to roll defaults account-wide tomorrow at 09:00 PT after 24h canary. objections?

leo: no objections. maybe include a note in release notes about the latency vs memory tradeoff.

priya: will add an entry to the onboarding docs and include the quick config snippet and reasoning.

maria: thanks all. marking this thread resolved unless we see regressions. :tada:
